summary: BBN explains the sizes of TIP message buffers in response to complaints that they were too small. It gives buffer sizes by device number in each direction and explains how users can set the TIP to send full-length messages.

plainLanguage.summary: TIP devices get buffers of different sizes, with lower-numbered devices receiving more space. Users can adjust when a message is sent to make better use of the buffer.

questions: how to optimize tip message length
subtitle: How TIP buffer sizes and send settings vary by device

tldr.problem: Users had complained about TIP message buffers, so BBN explains the available sizes and the limits behind them.
tldr.mechanism: Each device number has fixed input and output buffer sizes, and users can choose when a TIP sends accumulated characters.
tldr.outcome: The note recommends using lower-numbered devices and settings that allow longer messages when a host prefers them.

today: RFC 297 explains the TIP buffer arrangement and user settings used at the time. It presents buffer sizing as a trade-off within a limited total amount of space.

sections.title: Buffer Sizes Depend on Device Number
sections.content:
The note lists separate buffer sizes for messages going from a TIP to a host and from a host to a TIP. In both directions, lower-numbered devices have larger buffers. The specific sizes differ by direction and by device number.

TIP output is double-buffered: while one buffer is being printed, the TIP can receive data into another buffer.
sections.plainLanguage: Lower-numbered TIP devices have more room for messages than higher-numbered ones. The TIP can print one output buffer while preparing another.

sections.title: Choosing When to Send a Message
sections.content:
A TIP user can send each character immediately, wait for line feed or carriage-return conditions, send after a chosen number of characters, or combine the line-ending and character-count rules. Choosing a large character count lets the TIP build longer messages, up to the available buffer size.

The note suggests that hosts that prefer longer messages tell TIP users to select parameters that make use of the maximum buffer.
sections.plainLanguage: You can make the TIP send each character at once or wait and collect more first. Waiting can produce a longer message, up to the space available for that device.

sections.title: Why the Buffers Are Fixed
sections.content: The buffer sizes and their distribution can be changed if users suggest a better arrangement, but the total buffer space is limited. Each of the 63 devices needs two output buffers and one input buffer. The authors say that resizing buffers dynamically would require compaction and reclaiming space from current users, and estimate that this code would reduce the space available for buffers by about one-fifth.
sections.plainLanguage: The TIP has a fixed amount of memory for all its device buffers. Changing buffer sizes while it runs would take extra memory and could leave less room for messages overall.
